From the Editors

Optimum is all about financial discipline these days as it attempts to decrease costs in an environment of high debt and broadband subscriber losses.

For the second quarter, Optimum reported 40,000 broadband net subscriber losses. It now counts about 4 million broadband subs of which about 749,000 are fiber subscribers.

On its Q2 2026 earnings call Optimum’s CFO Marc Sirota said operating expense efficiencies are being driven by fewer truck rolls, fewer service phone calls, and salary cost reductions driven by workforce optimization via AI. “We are deploying additional tools and initiatives to further optimize operating expenses over time with a continued focus on enhancing the customer experience,” he said.

From the Editors

A couple months ago, when many of us were debating whether Elon Musk would get into terrestrial wireless by striking an MVNO pact, buying a mobile network operator or building his own network, industry analyst Roger Entner was firm in his belief: Musk will build, not buy, his way into wireless.

Based on SpaceX’s big reveal in its first-ever earnings conference call last week, Entner was right on the mark. What followed in the past week is plenty of speculation about just how Musk will pull this off. Musk and SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell provided enough ammunition to get the chatter going but stopped short of explaining exactly how they’re going to lure customers away from AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon with a better service.

They gave some hints, one being that Starlink could deploy something akin to femtocells on top of houses and other structures that are co-located with Starlink satellite dishes to provide terrestrial cellular coverage.

It was a busy weekend for Verizon engineers thanks to an outage that affected voice services for thousands of customers in some parts of the U.S. on Saturday.

Verizon didn’t reveal the cause of the outage but said the issue was resolved by around 4 p.m. Pacific time. At the time, the carrier advised customers who were still experiencing problems to restart their devices.

From the Editors

Zayo confirmed that its anchor tenant for 8,000 new route miles of fiber is Nvidia. The partners are building 16 new fiber routes in high-growth AI corridors across the U.S. Six of those routes are new (greenfield) routes, and 10 are overbuilds on existing Zayo fiber. In addition, Nvidia is also leasing fiber on eight other Zayo long-haul routes.

Bill Long, Zayo’s chief product and strategy officer, said building bulk fiber that will be used by multiple customers along the biggest power corridors in the U.S. “is a great business.”

Zayo’s CEO Steve Smith said fiber counts will vary by route. “On the popular routes, we're doing at least a 1,728. Our build packages can support 20,000 fibers a month from what we're putting in the ground today.”

entry.title: Registration Is Now Open 🎉
entry.content:
Join operators, vendors, and ecosystem leaders exploring the future of AI-RAN on September 9.
Register Now

Registration is now open!

Join us on September 9 for AI-RAN: Rewiring the Radio Network for the AI Era, a complimentary virtual summit from Fierce Network exploring how AI is rapidly moving from overlay to foundation in the radio access network (RAN)—redefining how mobile networks are built, operated, and monetized.

 

📅 September 9, 2026
🕚 11:00 a.m. – 3:30 p.m. ET

 

View the Agenda
Register for Free

AI-RAN represents a shift from single-purpose infrastructure to a converged, software-defined platform where AI and RAN workloads run side by side, enabling both real-time network optimization and entirely new classes of edge-based services.

 

For operators, the promise is compelling: improved spectral efficiency, more dynamic traffic management, and the ability to automate increasingly complex networks that can no longer be tuned manually. At the same time, AI-RAN opens a path to new revenue streams by turning the network into a distributed compute platform capable of supporting generative AI, enterprise applications, and emerging physical AI use cases at the edge.

 

But the transition is far from straightforward. Questions remain around cost, energy consumption, data readiness, and the real ROI of AI-native architectures. During this virtual event, operators, vendors, and ecosystem players will separate hype from execution, examining where AI is delivering measurable gains in the RAN today—and what it will take to scale AI-RAN into a commercially viable foundation for 5G Advanced and beyond.

 

Topics include:

  • Where are operators seeing tangible ROI today?
  • Which use cases are delivering the fastest returns?
  • How are deployment models evolving?
  • What are realistic timelines for ROI?

You'll also hear from industry leaders through keynote presentations and expert-led panel discussions, including:

 

From Trials to Reality: Where AI-RAN Is Delivering Today

The Business Case for AI-RAN: Cost, Complexity and Monetization

 

Don't miss this opportunity to hear how the industry is approaching AI-RAN today and what's next as AI becomes foundational to the future of the radio access network.

From the Editors

The direct-to-device (D2D) space is getting another boost from the Federal Communication Commission (FCC).

The FCC on Thursday voted to adopt a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to examine whether devices in the 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz bands should be able to communicate with satellites for D2D services. Devices operating in these unlicensed bands include Wi-Fi and Bluetooth transmitters.

An earlier draft NPRM called for the 900 MHz band to be included, but FCC staff said that band was removed in part because it proved to be “significantly more complex” than the other two bands.

From the Editors

Data center labor is scarce enough that operators now hire it away from one another, and Iron Mountain says the wage inflation that follows lands on customers.

“We end up hiring from each other and driving up wages, which isn't a bad thing for those that have [skills]," said Mark Kidd, EVP and GM of Iron Mountain's data center and asset lifecycle management businesses. "But it's not sustainable, because ultimately this cost gets passed back onto the user."

Operators are investing in college and trade school partnerships to address the shortage of electricians, technicians and mechanical specialists. Poaching is a more immediate solution to the problem, though it's one that drives up costs.

Read the full story here. – Linda Hardesty, Chief Analyst and Executive Editor

entry.title: Registration Is Now Open: AI-RAN: Rewiring the Radio Network for the AI Era
entry.content:
Join operators, vendors, and ecosystem leaders exploring the future of AI-RAN on September 9.
Register Now

Registration is now open!

Join us on September 9 for AI-RAN: Rewiring the Radio Network for the AI Era, a complimentary virtual summit from Fierce Network exploring how AI is rapidly moving from overlay to foundation in the radio access network (RAN)—redefining how mobile networks are built, operated, and monetized.

 

📅 September 9, 2026
🕚 11:00 a.m. – 3:30 p.m. ET

 

View the Agenda
Register for Free

AI-RAN represents a shift from single-purpose infrastructure to a converged, software-defined platform where AI and RAN workloads run side by side, enabling both real-time network optimization and entirely new classes of edge-based services.

 

For operators, the promise is compelling: improved spectral efficiency, more dynamic traffic management, and the ability to automate increasingly complex networks that can no longer be tuned manually. At the same time, AI-RAN opens a path to new revenue streams by turning the network into a distributed compute platform capable of supporting generative AI, enterprise applications, and emerging physical AI use cases at the edge.

 

But the transition is far from straightforward. Questions remain around cost, energy consumption, data readiness, and the real ROI of AI-native architectures. During this virtual event, operators, vendors, and ecosystem players will separate hype from execution, examining where AI is delivering measurable gains in the RAN today—and what it will take to scale AI-RAN into a commercially viable foundation for 5G Advanced and beyond.

 

Topics include:

  • Where are operators seeing tangible ROI today?
  • Which use cases are delivering the fastest returns?
  • How are deployment models evolving?
  • What are realistic timelines for ROI?

You'll also hear from industry leaders through keynote presentations and expert-led panel discussions, including:

 

From Trials to Reality: Where AI-RAN Is Delivering Today

The Business Case for AI-RAN: Cost, Complexity and Monetization

 

Don't miss this opportunity to hear how the industry is approaching AI-RAN today and what's next as AI becomes foundational to the future of the radio access network.

 

Reserve your complimentary spot today.
